lawyer:
Md Kaisar Ali, Advocate ----- For the Appellant. 
ABM Waliur Rahman Khan Assistant Attorney- General with Md Jalaluddin, Assistant Attorney- General ----- For the State.
full_judgment: 19. Mr Md Kowsar Ali submits that in this case there is no eye-witness of commission of murder. In the first information report the informant mentioned the name of Abdul Jabbar only, which called and took away the deceased. She did not mention the names of any other accused persons but to make an embellishment some witnesses including informant herself stated the name of the appellant along with the names of other accused persons implicating them in this case along with Abdul Jabbar and the deceased bad no enmity or transaction with the convict appellant herein and there might have been some enmity with Abdul Jabbar but the convict appellant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case and he further submits that PW 2, 4 and 5 stated that the present appellant was with Abdul Jabbar while he called and took away Mohammad Ali to his house. PW 6 one of the Union Parishad members stated that PW 1 stated to him that all the accused persons called and took away Abdul Jabbar at the relevant time and PW 3 the maidservant of Abdul Jabbar stated that she saw deceased Mohammad Ali along with all the accused persons ie Abdul Jabbar, Bhola, Shamsuddin and Abdus Sohban sitting in the Baranda of the dwelling house of Abdul Jabbar and they were discussing something. It may happen that while Abdul Jabbar and Mohammad Ali were sitting there the appellant and other accused persons might have gone there but this fact does not indicate that, they were involved in the commission of murder of the deceased. In this connection the learned Advocate referred to a decision reported in 33 DLR 320 Ismail Saker alias Sudan Member and others vs The State: Wherein it was held that deceased was last seen in the company of the accused at 10 PM followed by discovery of the dead body at noon next day. No presumption without further materials, that the accused was concerned in murder of the deceased. Circumstantial evidence being not incompatible with accused's innocence.
